Registry Entry
**Registry Entry**

A Registry Entry is a formal record maintained within the fictional reference world’s registry system. It serves as a generic yet comprehensive repository for relational data, documenting assertions, relationships, and information about other entries or subregions. Each entry captures a stated relationship between two identifiers, providing a structured description of how those entities are connected. The record may include source assertions indicating the provenance of the information, and it can encompass details about subregions and their specific relationships. In particular, a Registry Entry records the relationship between two subregions and may also record a source assertion about the relationship between a subregion and its parent region. Overall, the entry functions as a record that describes the relationship between two identifiers while documenting any associated source assertions and additional information about the involved entities.<SEP>An abstract representation of a record in a registry system.

Fictional Reference World
The Fictional Reference World is an imagined, conceptual setting that serves as the backdrop for registry entries and their relationships. It functions as a constructed reference frame within which subregions, registry entries, and their interconnections are defined, providing a consistent context for describing and organizing the registry’s contents. This hypothetical or illustrative setting is employed for fictional references, allowing registry entries to be situated in a coherent, yet purely conceptual, environment. The world is described as a conceptual setting that exists solely within the registry context, referred to as the current fictional reference world, and is used to contextualize the registry entries and their relationships.<SEP>A fictional world referenced by the registry entry.<SEP>An imagined setting referenced within the registry entry.<SEP>A constructed world used for reference purposes in the registry.<SEP>A conceptual world used for illustrative purposes in the text.

Source Assertion
Source Assertion

A Source Assertion is a statement recorded by a registry entry that serves as the source of information. It is a conceptual assertion documented within the registry entry itself and is not evaluated against other registry entries or entries. The assertion stands alone, providing a reference point for the information it conveys without comparison or validation against additional data. It is an assertion recorded by the registry entry that is not evaluated against other entries, and it serves as the source of information without evaluation of other entries. The assertion recorded by the registry entry is recorded as the source in the registry entry.<SEP>An assertion that originates from a source without evaluation of other entries.<SEP>A statement asserting a source without evaluating other entries.
